question: Compute the standard error of the mean when sigma = 3 and n = 36.
answer: The standard error of the mean is 0.5 [S1] [S2]. This is derived from the formula for standard error of the mean, which is sigma divided by the square root of n [S3]. Here, sigma = 3 and n = 36, so standard error = 3 / sqrt(36) = 0.5 [S1] [S2] [S3].

citations.title: Statistics Exercise Guide
citations.text:
Problem 3: Confidence Interval for a Mean
Question. A sample of n = 36 students has mean study time 12.4 hours per week. The population standard deviation is known to be 3 hours. Build a 95% confidence interval.
Solution. The standard error is 3 / sqrt(36) = 0.5. The margin of error is 1.96 * 0.5 = 0.98. The interval is 12.4 plus or minus 0.98, that is (11.42, 13.38). Interpretation: the procedure captures the true mean in about 95% of repeated samples. If the sample size were four times larger (n = 144) the standard error would halve to 0.25 and the interval would become narrower.

citations.title: Statistics Estimators And Bias
citations.text:
2. Variance of an Estimator
The variance of an estimator describes how much the estimate changes from one random sample
to the next. For the sample mean it equals sigma squared divided by n, so the standard error of the
mean is sigma divided by the square root of n.
This is not the same quantity as the variance of the data themselves, which describes the spread
of individual observations around their mean. Quadrupling the sample size halves the standard
error but does not change the variance of the data.

S5.title: Statistics Reference Notes
S5.text:
DISTRIBUTIONS
Binomial: P(X = k) = C(n, k) * p^k * (1 - p)^(n - k)
Poisson: P(X = k) = e^(-lambda) * lambda^k / k!
Normal z-score: z = (x - mu) / sigma
Empirical rule: 68% within 1 sigma, 95% within 2 sigma, 99.7% within 3 sigma.
Standard error of the mean: SE = sigma / sqrt(n)
